fields.label: Persoon toegang geven tot afgeschermde deel van de portal(s)

notes: Rebuilt 19-08-2026 on Taroen's steer — an update-and-insert against the debiteur's own connector, not a two-call chain. The earlier design (this same day) had it backwards: two separate top-level connectors, `KnPerson` then standalone `KnContact`, joined by fetching `BcCo` back from the first call to feed `BcCoPer` on the second. Taroen pointed at `KnSalesRelationOrg`/`KnPurchaseRelationOrg` instead, since live `GET metainfo/update/KnSalesRelationOrg` shows they already nest `KnOrganisation` → `KnContact` → `KnPerson` (`KnBankAccount`/`KnBasicAddressAdr`/`KnBasicAddressPad` besides). That nested `KnContact` has no `BcCoOga`/`BcCoPer` at all — it doesn't need them, because it's *positionally* nested inside the one organisation the parent `KnSalesRelationOrg` record already identifies. So the whole payload is **one call**: `PUT` to `KnSalesRelationOrg`, `@DbId` = the row's `Debiteur/Crediteur nummer` (this connector's own primary key — confirmed `primaryKey: true` live, matching an **existing** debiteur, no `BcCo` lookup or assumption needed at all, which retires that entire blocker from the previous design), `KnOrganisation` passed through with **no `Fields`** (it already exists; this payload only reaches through it), and a new `KnContact` **inserted** under it carrying the business-card fields, itself carrying a new `KnPerson` **inserted** under it carrying the name + address fields. Per-object `@Action` (`insert`/`update`/`delete`, docs §3.2/§4) is what makes 'touch only the new contact, leave the existing debiteur alone' possible on one PUT.

`@Action` per object is not something `MappingFieldModel` has a slot for — this mapping only says which field goes where, not insert-vs-update per object. Whatever builds the real payload needs: `KnSalesRelationOrg` root `@Action: "update"` (matched via `@DbId`), `KnOrganisation` with no `Fields` and no `@Action` (pure pass-through), `KnContact` and `KnPerson` both `@Action: "insert"`. Flagging plainly rather than inventing a new mapping-schema field for a upload engine that doesn't exist yet.

`DbId` here plays a different role than it does in `erp-debiteuren-organisatie.json`: there it's a value being *set* on a brand-new debiteur; here it's the **match key** identifying an *existing* one (`@DbId` as the Element's key attribute per docs §3.1, not a `Fields` entry) — same field code, opposite direction. AFAS's own schema still marks it `mandatory: false` (primary keys read that way when they're supplied as the match attribute rather than a body field), but a row with no value here has nothing to match against and must be rejected upstream of AFAS, not left to AFAS's own validation.

This file only covers `Contact bij = D` rows. `Contact bij = C` rows go through the sibling file `erp-contactpersonen-crediteur.json` (`KnPurchaseRelationOrg`) instead — same shape, same columns, different root connector and (see that file's notes) one real schema difference. `Contact bij` itself stays out of `fields`: it only decides which of the two files a row's other columns feed, the same way `erp-debiteuren-organisatie.json`'s 'Organisatie of Persoon' switch column consumes branching logic rather than mapping to one.

`ViKc` (Soort contact) fixed 'PRS': confirmed present on `KnSalesRelationOrg`'s nested `KnContact` (live), same reasoning as the retired standalone-`KnContact` mapping — every row is read as 'a person at that organisation'.

`AddToPortal` fixed false, `PadAdr` (on both `KnContact` and `KnPerson`) fixed true, `ResZip` fixed false (13-10-2026: the sheet now carries `Plaats (persoon)`, mapped to `Rs` and checked against the Woonplaatsen codetabel, as Debiteuren does), `MatchPer` left unmapped (business decision between always-insert and a naming-based dedupe match), `SeNm` capped at 10 characters, `HmNr` a strict `int` with no toevoeging column, `BeginDate` left unmapped as ignored-on-first-address — all carried over unchanged from the retired standalone mappings' reasoning; see git history on `erp-contactpersonen-persoon.json`/`erp-contactpersonen-contact.json` (removed this same day) for the fuller versions of each of these notes if needed.

Left unmapped on the nested `KnContact`: `ViFu` (controlled functie list — `Functienaam` goes to free-text `FuDs` instead, per the sjabloon's own 'tekst' label), `Corr`, `ViMd`, `FaNr`, `HoPa`, `Re`, `Bl`, `AtLn`, `LeHe`, `SocN`, `Face`, `Link`, `Twtr`. Left unmapped on the nested `KnPerson`: everything the retired standalone-`KnPerson` mapping already listed (no initials column, no BSN/geboorte/burgerlijke-staat data in this sjabloon, KnPerson's own phone/e-mail fields unused since the sheet's contact-detail columns are business-card fields on `KnContact` instead, etc.).

Ordering constraint unchanged: this `PUT` only succeeds against a debiteur that already exists, so a client's contactpersonen conversion can only run after their debiteuren conversion has landed. See docs/todo.md.

`erp-contactpersonen` has no deeltaakcode in AFAS, so this module cannot appear for a project today — groundwork, same as before. No upload engine exists yet to run per-object `@Action` from a stored mapping at all (`/api/upload` hands the whole sheet to Nymbus's own workflow) — see docs/todo.md.
Not grouped: one contactpersoon row produces one inserted KnContact + KnPerson pair, nested under the one existing debiteur the row names.

verifiedAgainst.description: Live GET metainfo/update/KnSalesRelationOrg via /api/afas/updateconnectors/modules/KnSalesRelationOrg — root/name 'KnSalesRelationOrg', `DbId` confirmed primaryKey. Nested tree: KnOrganisation → {KnBankAccount, KnBasicAddressAdr, KnBasicAddressPad, KnContact → {KnBasicAddressAdr, KnBasicAddressPad, KnPerson → {KnBankAccount, KnBasicAddressAdr, KnBasicAddressPad}}}. KnContact here has no BcCoOga/BcCoPer (unlike the standalone KnContact connector) — it doesn't need them, being positionally nested under the one KnOrganisation this KnSalesRelationOrg record already identifies.
